description: Baseline: Armenia is a Horizon Europe associated country, so the EIC Accelerator is open to an Armenian SME on equal terms
Armenia is a Horizon Europe 'widening' country, so the EIC Pre-Accelerator (TRL4-5, €300-500k) is open
Armenian national science funding (HESC) is reachable through an Armenian research institute partner
HESC's 2026 Remote Laboratories / Integration grants let a foreign PI build a group in Armenia — usable to bring a diaspora medicinal chemist
FAST ADVANCE research grants pair international scientists with Armenian groups — a route to fund wet-lab validation
ANSEF small grants fund Armenian researchers' stipends — usable by Denovo scientists as individuals
Armenia's ISTC membership gives access to the 2026 ISTC–Japan joint research call (biosafety/biosecurity priority fits antivirals)
Armenian Ministry of High-Tech Industry startup schemes provide direct grants
EU4Innovation East Armenia calls fund startups directly
Horizon Europe Cluster 1 (Health) collaborative calls — drug discovery, AMR and pandemic-preparedness topics — accept Armenian partners
Innovative Health Initiative (IHI JU) funds SMEs from associated countries in public-private drug-R&D consortia
EIT Health Catapult accepts startups from Horizon-associated countries (needs ≥€0.5M raised — Denovo reports ~$1.3M)
Antibiotic programme → CARB-X funds AMR therapeutics companies worldwide, incl. 'novel chemistry against validated targets'
Gates Grand Challenges periodically fund AI/novel-chemistry antibiotic and LMIC drug discovery, open worldwide
US DoD CDMRP allows foreign for-profit applicants by default — programmes cover rare disease, cancer, infectious disease
NIH research project grants (R01/R21) accept foreign organisations, incl. companies; a US partner (Emory/UCSD) can also subaward
NIH SBIR/STTR is the largest US small-business pool — but requires a US-owned, US-based company
Leukemia & Lymphoma Society TAP funds biotech companies (incl. non-US precedent) for blood-cancer therapeutics
Wellcome Discovery Awards: Armenia (UMIC) is eligible under current rules for applications submitted by 28 Oct 2026
Global Health EDCTP3 funds infectious-disease drug R&D with associated-country partners
Bayer Grants4Targets funds novel targets from start-ups worldwide in oncology, cardio, haematology, ophthalmology
Homocystinuria programme → HCU Network America/Australia fund new HCU therapies (academic PI; WCM-Q/Sidra could lead)
Rare-disease foundations: NORD's research grant programme funds international researchers per-disease
Penn Orphan Disease Center Million Dollar Bike Ride pilot grants fund international rare-disease research
ADDF Drug Development RFP funds biotech companies worldwide (mission-related investment)
Global Innovation Fund backs for-profit innovators worldwide via grants
AI-first startups get large cloud credit grants — Google for Startups Cloud AI tier
AWS Activate gives up to $100k credits to startups worldwide (more via accelerator 'Activate Provider' org IDs)
Microsoft for Startups (Founders Hub) offers Azure credits incl. GPU, open globally
NVIDIA Inception gives AI startups GPU/cloud credit offers and DGX Cloud discounts
J&J Innovation QuickFire Challenges give non-dilutive awards to global innovators
Merck KGaA Research Grants are open to company scientists worldwide; 2026 topics include SYNTHIA-based molecule synthesis
CF Foundation Therapeutics Development Awards explicitly welcome non-US companies (incl. antibacterials vs CF airway pathogens)
GHIT Fund finances anti-infective discovery if a Japanese partner and an MMV/DNDi/TB Alliance partner are on board
BARDA BAA (open to 2028) funds antiviral medical countermeasures; foreign companies can propose
Hevolution funds ageing biology/drug discovery worldwide
HESC bilateral calls (Italy CNR, Moldova, France PHC Ararat…) fund joint projects through Armenian institutes
Michael J. Fox Foundation funds companies worldwide for Parkinson's therapeutics
Children's Tumor Foundation funds NF drug discovery by companies worldwide
Antiviral programme → Pandemic Antiviral Discovery (Novo Nordisk Fdn/Gates/Open Phil) funds commercial orgs internationally, up to $10M
EuroHPC AI Factories give free GPU time to AI SMEs/startups in EU & associated countries — direct compute subsidy for generative chemistry
Anthropic AI for Science gives API credits to life-science researchers
One Health AMR partnership JTC funds companies in multinational AMR-treatment consortia
Horizon Europe Cluster 4 GenAI4EU booster challenges target generative AI in drug development
MSCA Staff Exchanges fund secondments between Denovo and academic partners (EU + worldwide)
MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships can be hosted by companies in associated countries — funds a postdoc at Denovo
MSCA Doctoral Networks (industrial doctorates) fund PhD students co-hosted by SMEs
Rare inborn-errors-of-metabolism foundations (PKU, cystinosis) fund academic PIs internationally — partner route for metabolic programme
Deep-tech competitions with cash prizes are open to Armenian startups (Hello Tomorrow, MIT Solve)
INCATE gives non-dilutive funding to early-stage antibacterial projects in Europe
Armenian EIF matching grants (World Bank/EU legacy) co-finance startups
Qatar partner (Sidra/WCM-Q) unlocks QRDI national research programme funding, with Denovo as international collaborator
Armenia is a widening country → Horizon Excellence Hubs (deadline 4 Mar 2027) can include Denovo and cascade up to €60k to startups
Oncology discovery funders that accept PIs worldwide (Worldwide Cancer Research) — company joins as collaborator
COST Actions reimburse Armenian participants (networking, STSMs) — cheap access to EU drug-discovery networks
Pharma AI-model access programmes give free in-kind resources (Lilly TuneLab, Boehringer opnMe)
EBRD Star Venture supports locally-owned Armenian startups (non-cash)
ARPA-H can fund foreign entities directly in some solicitations (e.g. AI-for-research programmes)
EIC Pathfinder: Open needs a 3-country consortium (next 2027); Challenges (deadline 28 Oct 2026) allow single applicants
BE READY pandemic-preparedness partnership funds therapeutic-target work on priority virus families
Malaria/NTD product-development partnerships (MMV) fund drug-discovery partners worldwide incl. computational work
Coefficient Giving (ex-Open Philanthropy) Science & Global Health R&D funds preclinical drug work
Cancer Grand Challenges: join a team as the AI-chemistry partner
GARDP has open antibiotic-discovery partnerships for companies
NATO SPS is open to partner country Armenia; 2027-1 call (deadline 15 Nov 2026) includes CBRN defence — medical countermeasures
Wellcome Leap programmes accept any legal entity in any jurisdiction, companies included
FAST's B-On Biotech Prototyping Lab gives Armenian biotech teams shared wet-lab space — in-kind support for assay validation
Oncology foundations funding international academic teams (PCF Challenge Awards) — partner route
ICGEB Collaborative Research Programme grants (€25k/yr) — if Armenia is a member state
Novo Holdings REPAIR Impact Fund backs early AMR companies
FDA Orphan Products grants accept foreign for-profit applicants — route for a future HCU clinical study with Sidra
Korea's RIGHT Foundation mirrors GHIT: global-health product development with a Korean partner
Entrepreneurship World Cup — Denovo was a 2021 global finalist; ~$1M equity-free prizes yearly incl. AI subtrack
ERDERA rare-disease joint calls — Armenia not found among funding countries
AstraZeneca open innovation gives compound-library and target-collaboration access
Subsidiary routes: Innovate UK and India's BIRAC fund only locally registered companies (Mankind Pharma tie-in for India)
Compute access for research partners: Google TPU Research Cloud, Oracle for Startups credits
LLS Translational Research Program funds non-US academic PIs on blood cancers — oncology partner route
WHO/TDR impact grants fund infectious-disease research in LMICs
Grand Challenges Canada lists Armenia as eligible LMIC for Stars in Global Health
Individual fellowships let Denovo scientists spend time in partner labs (Humboldt, Fulbright)
Armenian Ministry of High-Tech + Plug and Play Germany acceleration is a non-cash route to EU pharma partners
ITU AI for Good Innovation Factory gives AI startups global exposure
AACR research grants accept international academic investigators — oncology partner route
DNDi funds hit-to-lead partners and runs the Drug Discovery Booster for neglected diseases
Academic compute programmes reach Denovo via university collaborators (AWS research credits, NVIDIA academic grants)
EuroHPC 'AI for Science' access mode is open to industry in associated countries for open research
Pfizer Global Medical Grants run competitive research RFPs open worldwide
CPRIT product-development awards are large but require operating in Texas
Disease venture-philanthropies fund companies worldwide for new therapeutics (T1D, IBD, MS) — open doors if Denovo adds a programme
Rare metabolic/lysosomal disease foundations also fund international researchers and biotechs (Sanfilippo, mitochondrial)
NIH's AViDD antiviral centres funded pandemic small-molecule discovery
USAID innovation grants in Armenia
EIC Transition could take Denovo's platform to market as a single SME
Verify: One Health AMR JTC — partners are funded only by participating national funders; Armenia is not one
Verify: EuroHPC access policy covers industry established in Horizon Europe associated countries; drop zero-value Neruzh record
Verify: NIH accepts foreign (incl. for-profit) applicants for research project grants, but not SBIR/STTR, centres or training grants
Alzheimer's Association Part the Cloud funds companies worldwide for neurodegeneration drug programmes
TB/neurodegeneration product-development partners fund external chemistry (TB Alliance via GHIT; Parkinson's UK Virtual Biotech)
SSIEM (inborn errors of metabolism society) offers research grants relevant to homocystinuria
Verify (run 2): a majority non-US-owned Delaware parent with no US operations is still SBIR/STTR-ineligible
Verify (run 2): the US parent can apply to NIH as a domestic for-profit; Armenian work is a foreign component needing prior approval
Verify (run 2): BARDA BAA accepts any responsible US source registered in SAM.gov — the US parent qualifies
Verify (run 2): EIC applicant must be the Armenian LLC; the US parent's headcount/finances count toward SME status
US in-kind: NIAID preclinical services (incl. Antiviral Program for Pandemics) serve industry at domestic or foreign institutions
US in-kind: NCATS TRND partners with for-profit (incl. foreign) companies on orphan diseases — homocystinuria qualifies
NCI NExT gives oncology drug-development resources to companies
NCATS BrIDGs provides IND-enabling studies to companies
BARDA DRIVe EZ-BAA gives the US parent fast awards up to ~$750k
US-based affiliates of foreign companies can join DoD medical-countermeasure OTA consortia (MCDC) and bid on prototype projects
